claims.reason_summary: Compression gives Λ≥λ>0, and |Λ−λ|≤e gives normalized-generator distance ≤2e/Λ≤2e/λ. Duhamel multiplies this by |τ|. For either state, output probability L1 change is ≤2‖U−U₀‖op, so utility change is ≤Δ‖U−U₀‖op. Under U₀ the utility excluding bias is exactly a mixture of the retained-only utility and the native nuisance mean with weights 1−δ and δ. This adds at most δΔ, yielding (1).

The Hermitian cross-block has norm ‖C‖op≤‖C‖F≤√(rm)η^q. The nuisance principal block has norm ≤(m−1)η^q by absolute row sums. The retained two-key compression has norm at least ρ^q. These give (2), including when m=1.

Both bias-free logits are convex averages in the same utility interval, so their difference is independently capped by Δ and the stated C_r is valid. Log-sum-exp is 1-Lipschitz in the infinity norm; subtracting the target logit adds at most C_y, giving (3). Each retained winner–competitor gap can shrink by at most C_k+C_r, so the strict margin condition preserves the unique winner.

For the stated interface, εI is invariant under U, giving exactly the coherent post-evolution floor. In the dephased case, output i receives Σ_j |U_ij|²(|a_j|²+ε)/D, matching the row-vector transpose convention. Under U₀ the retained denominator divided by D equals 1−δ; coherent cross-block terms need not vanish as a matrix but do not enter the measured diagonal.

For η<ρ the cubic transport upper envelope is smaller than the linear envelope, not necessarily the actual perturbation or even the measured e_q/λ_q. The result singles out the affinity exponent, not coherence: the initially dephased route has the same guarantee. Neither task improvement nor novelty follows.

scope_limits: Mapping is conditional on the supplied interface, not independent source verification. The comparison fixes features, queries, utilities and bias and assumes λ_q>0.
Graph separation does not bound query mass δ. For Δ_r>0 the logit certificate improves on the utility-range cap only if δ_r+2|τ|e_q/λ_q<1; even then it need not certify a prediction.
